paragraphs: On Saturday morning, the Explorers went to a music festival at the town stadium. Each child had a ticket and a green paper flag. The stadium was enormous, and it was full of people. Teacher Kim stopped the group at the gate.

"Listen to the rules," she said. "If you hear this tune, come to the big green flag." She played a short tune on a small whistle. "If you cannot find us, stay at the gate and ask a guard." "If a stranger talks to you, you come to me." "Does everybody understand?" "Yes, Teacher Kim," said the children.

The festival was noisy and bright. There was a band on a big stage, and many children danced. Mia loved the music, so she stopped to dance near the stage. Lily, Leo, and May walked on to look at the food stalls. Suddenly, Mia looked around, and she could not see her friends. She stood still and thought about the rules. "What happens now?" she asked herself.

A tall boy next to Mia laughed at her paper flag. "Your flag is silly," he said, and that was unkind. Mia did not answer, and she did not run away. She listened carefully to the noise of the festival. At the flag, Teacher Kim counted the children. Mia was not there. Teacher Kim took out her whistle. She played the tune. Then Mia heard a short tune from a whistle. "That is our tune!" said Mia, and she smiled. She walked quickly to the big green flag.

Teacher Kim and the three friends waited at the flag. "I am here," said Mia. "I stopped when I could not find you, and I listened for the tune." "Well done, Mia," said Teacher Kim kindly. "If you follow the rules, everybody is safe." Leo gave Mia a cold drink, and May held her hand. Then the group walked to the stage, and the Explorers danced together until the end.
text.summary: The Explorers visit a music festival at the town stadium. Teacher Kim gives rules with if, and Mia uses the rule about the tune when she loses the group.
